elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Both 12.1.1 and the inserted IP paragraph say only "indemnify and hold ... harmless" / "will also indemnify the PB Indemnified Parties"; no express "defend" obligation was added. Repair: insert "defend" into the operative verb string ("SFJ will defend, indemnify and hold harmless the PB Indemnified Parties ...").

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 12.1.1 runs to "PB; its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees and agents (the "PB Indemnified Parties")" for "Claims by a Third Party"; the inserted paragraph indemnifies the same defined group.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "any Claim by a Third Party alleging that any services, materials or deliverables provided by SFJ or any of its Affiliates or Permitted Third Parties infringe or misappropriate the Intellectual Property of a Third Party".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The rendered 12.1.1 heads reach gross negligence/wilful misconduct and (per the cited heads) material breach, Protocol breach, AZ License breach, post-transfer subject injury and product liability; no head references breach of applicable law, and no such head was added.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No operative language in 12.1.1 or the inserted paragraph addresses unauthorised access to or disclosure of PB data caused by SFJ.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: 12.1.1(a): "the gross negligence or willful misconduct of SFJ or any of its Affiliates or any of its or their respective Permitted Third Parties in performing SFJ's obligations under this Agreement".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Article 12.2 (defined "Indemnified Party" per 1.1.92 referencing Section 12.2.1) contains the notice mechanic and is retained unchanged; the new indemnity sits within Article 12 and inherits it.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Existing Article 12.2 procedure (control of defence) is unchanged and applies to Article 12 indemnities.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Existing Article 12.2 cooperation requirement is retained unchanged.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 12.1.2 still obliges PB to indemnify SFJ for Product supplied by PB, PB's material breach, Protocol breach, infringement by the Product, and Subject injuries/Commercialization claims "(a) through (g)" — far broader than PB-provided content plus PB's breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence in 12.1.1: "SFJ will also indemnify the PB Indemnified Parties from any and all Losses arising or resulting from any Claim by a Third Party alleging that any services, materials or deliverables provided by SFJ ... infringe or misappropriate the Intellectual Property of a Third Party"; the conforming cut to 12.1.2(f) removes the contradictory PB indemnity for infringement "by either Party".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: "except to the extent such Claim arises from PB's modification of such items".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: "PB's combination of such items with items not supplied by SFJ".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "SFJ will procure for PB the right to continue using the infringing item, or modify or replace it so that it is non-infringing".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of the foregoing is available on commercially reasonable terms, refund the amounts paid by PB to SFJ for such item" — express fallback refund tied to unavailability of the other remedies.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "SFJ's liability under this paragraph will not exceed three (3) times the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months preceding the Claim" — a 3x multiple of a twelve-month (annual) payment base; the broader "amounts paid or payable" base is customer-favourable relative to "fees".

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: an SFJ third-party IP indemnity, the three customary exclusions (PB modification, PB combination, PB specifications), the procure/modify/replace ladder with a refund backstop, and a 3x twelve-month super-cap all appear in operative language.

The preferred level is incomplete on four elements: no express duty to defend, no breach-of-applicable-law head, no Vendor-caused data-breach head, and PB's indemnity in 12.1.2 remains broad rather than limited to PB-provided content and PB's breach of law. The drafter's decision not to pursue the preferred level is stated and consistent with the rendered text.

Minimality holds. The insertion is a concise new paragraph, and the only deletion — "or by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder with respect to the Product" in 12.1.2(f) — is a necessary conforming cut: retaining it would have left PB indemnifying SFJ for SFJ's own infringement, a contradictory retained clause that would nullify the new SFJ IP indemnity. Nothing else in Article 12 (heads (a)-(g), the carve-backs, the tax-benefit netting, the Article 12.2 procedure) was touched.

Intent is preserved: the negotiated subject-injury, Protocol, Program Transfer and product-liability allocations, the existing procedure cross-references and the defined terms (PB Indemnified Parties, Losses, Claim, Intellectual Property, Third Party) all survive without dangling references.

Actionable drafting risk to raise even though the elements are formally met: the refund remedy and the 3x super-cap are both keyed to "amounts paid by PB to SFJ" / "paid or payable by PB to SFJ ... during the twelve (12) months preceding the Claim." In this Agreement the funding flow runs predominantly SFJ to PB, with PB's payments to SFJ concentrated post-approval, so during the Clinical Trial period both the refund and the cap could compute to zero and render the new indemnity illusory. Consider re-basing the cap on amounts paid or payable by SFJ under the Agreement in the preceding twelve months (or a stated dollar floor) and re-basing the refund on amounts paid for the affected services, materials or deliverables however funded.

Secondary point for the same paragraph: the cap is anchored to the twelve months preceding "the Claim" rather than the event giving rise to the Claim; if the playbook prefers the event anchor, that wording should be conformed.

If the preferred position is later pursued, the minimum operative repairs are: add "defend" to the indemnity verbs, add heads for SFJ's breach of applicable law and for unauthorised access to or disclosure of PB data caused by SFJ, and narrow 12.1.2 to PB-supplied content and PB's breach of law.
